docs.menu.a11y.dialog: Inside a modal Dialog the menu opens in the dialog, so it is in the top layer and can be pressed. The first Escape closes only the menu and the second one closes the dialog.
docs.menu.a11y.disabled: A disabled item has aria-disabled: it is announced as unavailable and the arrow keys skip it. Use note to say why.
docs.menu.a11y.focus: When the menu closes the focus goes back to the trigger. Tab closes it and the focus moves on from the trigger, so it never ends on the page body. Pressing outside closes it and the focus stays where it was pressed.
docs.menu.a11y.keyboard: The down arrow opens the menu on its first item and the up arrow on its last. Inside, the arrows move between the items and wrap around, Home and End go to the first and the last, a letter goes to the first item that starts with it, Enter and Space select, and Escape closes.
docs.menu.a11y.name: An item is named by its label alone. The second line is its description (aria-describedby) and a leading box is decoration, so a screen reader does not read the role as a part of the name.
docs.menu.a11y.options: An item with checked is a menuitemradio with aria-checked: one option of a group is chosen. Several independent options are not covered, see the limitations.
docs.menu.a11y.pattern: It follows the ARIA menu button pattern: the trigger has aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded, the list is a role="menu" named by label, and its items are menuitem.
docs.menu.a11y.search: The search field is outside the role="menu" and takes the focus first. Escape clears its text and a second Escape closes the menu. When nothing matches, emptyText goes into a live region that was already in the menu, so it is announced.
docs.menu.a11y.strings: Menu has no text of its own: the labels, the note and the texts of the search come from your props, in your language.
docs.menu.a11y.trigger: The trigger has to be a control that takes the focus: a Button, an IconButton or a FilterChip. One with no text, such as an IconButton, needs a name of its own.
docs.menu.api.children: Receives the props of the trigger and returns the trigger element. Spread all of them on it: they are listed below.
docs.menu.api.items: The rows of the menu, in order. Each one is a MenuItem, listed below.
docs.menu.api.label: The accessible name of the menu.
docs.menu.api.note: An explanation under the list. The menu takes it as its description, so it is heard why an item is disabled.
docs.menu.api.placement: Where the menu goes relative to its trigger, aligned to its end or to its start. It flips above when it does not fit below.
docs.menu.api.search: A field that filters the items marked searchable. It sits above the list, outside the role="menu", and both of its texts come from the application.
docs.menu.api.wide: A wider menu, for rows with two lines.
docs.menu.group.search.description: A field above the list filters the items that opt in with searchable. The rest, such as the action at the foot, stay in view, and when nothing matches the menu says so.
docs.menu.group.search.title: Search
docs.menu.group.triggers.description: Any control that takes the focus can open a menu: spread what Menu gives you on it.
docs.menu.group.triggers.title: Triggers
docs.menu.hint.checked: The options of a group: the current one has a check and the menu opens on it. Each has a description under its name.
docs.menu.hint.default: A plain action, a separator and a destructive action. Open it with Enter or the down arrow, then move with the arrows, Home, End or the first letter of an item.
docs.menu.hint.disabled: The disabled item stays in the menu, and the arrow keys skip it.
docs.menu.hint.filterChip: A FilterChip is the trigger: it draws its chevron and is not a toggle, so its label carries the chosen value.
docs.menu.hint.iconButton: The more icon opens the menu of a row, and the label of the button is its name.
docs.menu.hint.note: The note describes the menu, so a screen reader says why the item is unavailable.
docs.menu.hint.search: The focus starts on the field. Type to filter, ignoring accents, and press the down arrow to go to the list.
docs.menu.item.checked: Makes the item an option of a group: true is the chosen one and shows a check, false the others. The role becomes menuitemradio and the menu opens on the chosen one. Your application keeps which one it is.
docs.menu.item.description: A second, smaller line under the label, such as the role in a workspace. It is the accessible description of the item, not a part of its name.
docs.menu.item.disabled: The item cannot be selected and the arrow keys skip it. It stays in the menu, announced as unavailable.
docs.menu.item.icon: An icon before the text, one of the library's icons.
docs.menu.item.id: A stable identifier of the item. It is the key of the row.
docs.menu.item.label: The text of the item, and its accessible name. A long label wraps on a plain item and is cut with … on an item that has a description.
docs.menu.item.leading: Decorative content before the text, such as an avatar. It is not part of the name: hide it from assistive technology.
docs.menu.item.onSelect: Called when the item is selected, after the menu has closed and the focus is back on the trigger.
docs.menu.item.searchable: The search field filters this item by its text. The items without it are always shown, such as an action at the foot of the list.
docs.menu.item.separatorBefore: Draws a separator before the item. A separator is not an item: the arrow keys skip it.
docs.menu.item.title: The full name for the pointer, for when a long label is cut with …
docs.menu.item.tone: danger colors a destructive action. Color alone does not say it: the label has to.
docs.menu.limit.checkbox: checked makes a menuitemradio. There is no menuitemcheckbox for several independent options, and the menu does not uncheck the others: your state does.
docs.menu.limit.items: The items are data. A row can only take a leading element, and there are no group headings.
docs.menu.limit.placement: There are two placements, below the trigger and aligned to its end or to its start. The menu flips above when it does not fit, but there is no way to ask for another side, an offset or an arrow.
docs.menu.limit.size: The menu is 200 px wide at least, 280 px when it is wide, and 320 px at most. Its list scrolls past 24 rem. The widths and the height of a row are the tokens --menu-min-width, --menu-min-width-wide, --menu-max-width and --menu-item-min-height.
docs.menu.limit.spread: What you spread replaces the ref, the onClick and the onKeyDown of the trigger. Call your own handlers from inside the ones that Menu gives you, and merge a ref yourself.
docs.menu.limit.touch: It is checked with axe and the keyboard in a real browser, not with a screen reader on each platform. Below 768 px each row is as tall as a touch target, 44 px.
docs.menu.search.emptyText: What the menu says, in a live region, when no searchable item matches.
docs.menu.search.label: The accessible name of the field, which is also its placeholder. The library has no text of its own for it.
docs.menu.search.title: The search field: MenuSearch
docs.menu.states.description: A menu opens from its trigger and gives the focus back to it when it closes. Each of these is the live component: open it and try the keyboard.
docs.menu.summary: A menu of actions that opens from a button, with the keyboard and an optional search.
docs.menu.trigger.ariaControls: The id of the menu while it is open, and nothing while it is closed.
docs.menu.trigger.ariaHaspopup: Says that the trigger opens a menu. A FilterChip draws its chevron when it sees it.
docs.menu.trigger.onKeyDown: Opens the menu with the down arrow, on its first item or the chosen one, and with the up arrow, on its last item.
docs.menu.trigger.ref: Registers the trigger as the anchor that the menu is placed against. It replaces a ref of your own: merge them yourself.
docs.menu.trigger.title: What Menu hands to its trigger: MenuTriggerProps
docs.menu.usage.description: Import Menu and spread what it gives you on the element that opens it. The items are data: each one says what it does when it is selected.
